examples.solution_text:
The logarithm returns the index because the bases match.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\log_{6}(6^{3t-2})\\&=3t-2\end{aligned}$

Raising the base to its logarithm returns the argument.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8^{\log_{8}6.4}\\&=6.4\end{aligned}$

Write the reciprocal as a negative power of the logarithm's base.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\log_{4}\frac{1}{4^{3}}\\&=\log_{4}(4^{-3})\\&=-3\end{aligned}$

Write the cube root as a fractional power, then use the inverse identity.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\log_{6}\sqrt[3]{6^{5}}\\&=\log_{6}(6^{\frac{5}{3}})\\&=\frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}$

Apply the inverse identity inside the product, keeping the coefficient.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}5\log_{3}(3^{4})\\&=5\times4\\&=20\end{aligned}$

The cube root gives a fractional index; the reciprocal makes it negative.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\log_{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{4^{7}}}\\&=\log_{4}(4^{-\frac{7}{3}})\\&=-\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: For base 6, the inverse identity returns the complete real index: log_6(6^(3t−2)) = 3t−2.
The outer base and logarithm base are both 8, and 6.4 is positive. Thus 8^(log_8 6.4) = 6.4.
The cube root of 6^5 is 6^(5/3). Applying log base 6 returns 5/3.
The cube root of 4^7 is 4^(7/3); its reciprocal is 4^(−7/3). Applying log base 4 returns −7/3.
